ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, authorized signatories and contemplated counterparties against the U.S. OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU/UK financial sanctions lists, Interpol notices, and the New Zealand consolidated sanctions list administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade under the United Nations Act 1946 and the Russia Sanctions Act 2022. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for identified Politically Exposed Persons, persons connected to high-risk jurisdictions, or where public-adverse-media indicators are identified; all screening results must be preserved in the AML/CFT clearance memorandum.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies Office – New Zealand Companies Register Online Services (register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be recorded in Latin script; Te Reo Māori and English names are permitted. Where a proposed name originates in a non-Latin script, a Latin-alphabet transliteration must be supplied, and the official name will be registered in transliterated form. Names that are identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, or otherwise misleading or contrary to public policy, will be rejected under the Companies Act 1993.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name approval cannot be extended; if the reservation lapses, the applicant may file a fresh name application. On rejection, the Companies Office issues a written refusal with the specific ground. The applicant may submit an internal administrative review to the Companies Office within 10 working days, attaching evidence of consent or clarification from the relevant statutory authority or regulator. If the internal review is unsuccessful, the applicant may seek judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand within 20 working days of the refusal decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted with limitations. The registered office must be a physical street address in New Zealand, not a P.O. Box or a purely virtual maildrop. A licensed virtual office provider may be used as the registered office and local agent, provided it accepts service of process, maintains statutory records, and is operational during ordinary business hours.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate – approximately 20% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection in the first 12 months under New Zealand AML/CFT risk-based supervision. If large-value wire transfers are executed without a financial-services licence or if third-party payment concentration is detected, the probability escalates to greater than 50%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), New Zealand, as consolidated; principally: sections 12 to 16 (incorporation, registration and certificate of incorporation), section 27 (constitution), sections 38 to 54 (capital, shares and no-par-value shares), sections 122 to 129 (board of directors' powers), sections 131 to 140 (directors' duties), section 151(2) (at least one New Zealand-resident director), and section 180 (registered office). New Zealand has no separate 'International Company' incorporation statute; the International Company (CK_IC) designation is an administrative and governance label recorded in the company constitution and shareholder documents, with legal personality derived solely from the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE); online filing through Companies Office Online using a RealMe verified identity.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 5 – Application for Registration of a Company (electronic filing in Companies Office Online), together with Form 6 – Company Name Reservation where a name reservation is lodged separately, and Form 2 – Consent to Appointment as Director; the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation and allocates a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) upon approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the Companies Act 1993. Shares may be issued with no par value for lawful consideration to be fixed by the board. No escrow account or upfront capital deposit is mandated. For the International Company status, the initial subscriber will subscribe one ordinary share at NZD 1.00 (fully paid) as nominal consideration; the company must maintain a registered office in New Zealand and at least one director resident in New Zealand.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [CK_IC] / [FUND NAME] LIMITED (the Company) adopted on [Date] at [Registered Office Address], New Zealand, pursuant to the Companies Act 1993. RESOLVED THAT: 1. CONSTITUTION: The registered Constitution of the Company tabled at this meeting is adopted as the Company's supreme internal governance instrument and shall be binding on the Company, its shareholders and directors under sections 26-29 of the Companies Act 1993. 2. SHARE ALLOTMENT: The initial subscriber is allotted one Ordinary Share with no par value at an issue price of NZD 1.00, fully paid, under sections 42-43 and 46 of the Companies Act 1993, and the share register is duly updated. The board confirms that New Zealand imposes no minimum paid-up capital requirement and that no escrow account is required. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office of the Company is fixed at [Street Address, Suburb, City, New Zealand], being a physical New Zealand address, and the directors are directed to notify the Registrar of any change in accordance with section 180 of the Companies Act 1993. 4. OFFICERS: [Name] is appointed as Managing Director, [Name] is appointed as Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] is appointed as Company Secretary (optional but permissible) and authorised signatory. 5. BANKING AND FUND OPERATIONS: The officers are authorised to open bank accounts, execute non-dilutive revenue-based financing agreements with digital-brand borrowers, receive payments via Direct Debit/ACH and Wire Transfer, and engage legal, tax and AML/CFT advisors. 6. TAX CLASSIFICATION: The Company shall operate as an international royalty and revenue-based financing fund (ISIC 6499 / NAICS 525990). The directors acknowledge that any Tax-Exempt Zone treatment depends on foreign-source income analysis and Inland Revenue rulings and authorises counsel to pursue those rulings in Stage 3. 7. LICENCE COMPLIANCE: The board confirms that the Company undertakes no industrial or physical manufacturing activity, that no environmental permit is required under the Resource Management Act 1991, and that fire safety and workplace compliance for the registered office will be secured before occupation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name availability search and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Office Online, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), via RealMe identity authentication
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a company name search on the New Zealand Companies Register to verify that the proposed name, including the 'Limited' suffix, is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered or reserved name under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993. File Form 6 (Company Name Reservation) online, or, to expedite the transaction, proceed directly with the incorporation application which includes the proposed name and up to alternate names. Retain the name reservation reference for use in the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and at least three alternate names
RealMe verified proof of identity of the applicant
Certificate of authority or power of attorney if the applicant acts as agent
Details of any translations, abbreviations or special characters used in the name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar refuses the name under sections 22 to 25, the applicant will receive a written notice. Counsel may request reconsideration within 20 working days, submit alternate names on the same application, obtain the written consent of the holder of a similar name, or apply to the High Court for judicial review where consent is withheld unreasonably.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and execution of constitution, director consents and governance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator's solicitors and authorised governance advisors; final documents will be lodged with the New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the company constitution under section 27 of the Companies Act 1993, incorporating special share class rights, the revenue-based financing object, and the International Company designation. Obtain each proposed director's written consent on Form 2 and each subscriber's irrevocable subscription letter. Verify that at least one director satisfies the New Zealand residence requirement under section 151(2). Arrange the registered office address consent from the premises owner and prepare the shareholder side letter setting out the non-dilutive royalty financing mandate.
required_dossiers: Form 2 – Consent to Appointment as Director for each director
Subscriber subscription letter and share application
Shareholders' side letter describing the non-dilutive revenue-based financing fund mandate
Registered office address consent from the premises owner
Identity documents and background declarations for directors and ultimate beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MBIE or the Registrar challenges any constitutional clause as incompatible with the Companies Act 1993, counsel will revise the constitution and resubmit. Where a director's consent is deficient, a corrected Form 2 must be executed and lodged. Registered office consent must be renewed if the address is rejected as not being a physical New Zealand address.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgement of Form 5 incorporation application with Companies Office Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into Companies Office Online using the RealMe authenticated account. Complete the 'Register a Company' electronic application (Form 5). Enter the reserved company name, company number from any name reservation, registered office address, principal place of business, director and shareholder details, and upload the constitution and Form 2 consents. The system will perform an automated name and statutory eligibility check. Pay the prescribed filing fee (approximately NZD 47.60, equivalent to about USD 29) by credit card or debit card and submit the application.
required_dossiers: Form 5 electronic data capture completed online
Form 6 name reservation reference if name was pre-reserved
Constitution in PDF format signed by the subscriber
RealMe identity verification records for directors and shareholders
Payment instrument for the incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query, a formal response must be filed within 10 working days, supported by corrected documents. If the application is refused, the incorporator may resubmit after curing the defect; any refusal grounded on statutory non-compliance may be appealed to the High Court under the Companies Act 1993.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand, Te Tari Taake; online portal: myIR (secure web portal and taxpayer digital services)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity, including an International Company formed under the Cook Islands International Companies Act, must apply for a New Zealand IRD number for company tax and GST purposes. The application is made via the myIR portal or by filing the relevant IRD application for non-resident companies (IR596 or equivalent), accompanied by certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, registered office certificate, director/shareholder information, and evidence of the entity's tax residence status. If the entity is not resident in New Zealand, it may still be required to register for GST if it carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand or supplies remote services to New Zealand consumers above the registration threshold. The IRD number is issued without a legal requirement for a local registered office, but a New Zealand agent or tax representative may be required for service of documents and compliance purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a check-the-box election comparable to the U.S. regime. Instead, the Income Tax Act 2007 provides for specific elections and deeming rules including: the election for look-through treatment for certain closely held companies (LTC election); the controlled foreign company (CFC) attribution election and active business exemption; the qualifying company election regime (now closed to new entrants); and the hybrid mismatch rules which contain elections to adjust the treatment of certain instruments and entities. The Cook Islands International Company is generally treated as a non-resident company, and New Zealand's territorial tax rules only subject it to income tax on certain New Zealand-sourced income, if it carries on a business through a New Zealand fixed establishment or has other statutory nexus.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST), a credit-invoice value-added tax administered under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (New Zealand)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in a 12-month period for goods and services supplied in New Zealand or imported remote services/digital goods supplied to New Zealand consumers; NZD 60,000 threshold for non-resident suppliers of remote services under the offshore supplier registration rules; voluntary registration permitted below threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No universal real-time fiscal clearance mandate or digital stamping system currently exists. New Zealand operates a voluntary e-invoicing framework aligned with the Peppol standard, and taxpayers are required to maintain sufficient electronic records in a format accessible to Inland Revenue. Tax invoices (including buyer-created tax invoices) must be issued within 28 days of the supply, or as agreed under a GST group election. Inland Revenue has increasingly mandated electronic filing of GST returns and supports API-based data exchange for payroll and tax information, but there is no transaction-by-transaction real-time fiscal clearance requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of exported goods under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 applies where goods are exported by the supplier, delivered to a carrier for direct export, or supplied to a non-resident for delivery outside New Zealand. Services supplied to non-residents may be zero-rated under section 11A where the services are supplied in relation to goods outside New Zealand, or are supplied in the course of a taxable activity and the services are not physically performed in New Zealand and the non-resident is outside New Zealand at the time of supply. An International Company engaged in royalty financing and revenue-based financing of digital brands may zero-rate offshore financing and ancillary services where the services are supplied to non-residents and the place of supply is outside New Zealand. Interest income and certain financial services are generally exempt (input-taxed) rather than zero-rated under GST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Export Entry (Customs Export Declaration) or electronic equivalent via the Trade Single Window
Commercial Invoice / Tax Invoice showing NZ GST number and zero-rating basis
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export of goods
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement proving receipt of foreign currency export proceeds
Underlying contract or royalty/financing agreement supporting the off-shore service supplied
Evidence of the non-resident status of the recipient (e.g., certificate of incorporation, tax residence certificate, or statutory declaration)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may audit zero-rated export supplies and require full documentary substantiation. Where a taxpayer fails to hold sufficient evidence that goods were exported or services were supplied to a non-resident, the supply is recharacterised as standard-rated and GST becomes payable at 15%, with late payment penalties and use-of-money interest applying from the original due date. Knowingly or negligently zero-rating ineligible supplies may attract a tax shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the resulting tax shortfall for abusive tax positions, and up to 100% for not taking reasonable care. Fraudulent GST refund claims and intentional evasion can lead to criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act 1994, imprisonment up to 5 years, and fines up to NZD 50,000 for individuals and NZD 250,000 for companies. The Commissioner may issue a Notice of Assessment clawing back refunds and, in significant cases, obtain freezing or charging orders over assets. There is no time bar where evasion or fraud is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua), exercising prudential supervision over Registered Banks, payment systems, and licensed non-bank deposit takers, acting alongside the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for market conduct, and the Department of Internal Affairs for the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act) supervisory framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is fully convertible under a free-floating exchange rate regime. There are no residual exchange controls under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989, and the Exchange Control Act 1953 has been fully repealed. Current account transactions (royalties, interest, dividends, trade payments, and profit remittances) and capital account transactions (foreign direct investment, intercompany loans, portfolio investment, and repatriation of invested capital) may be effected freely without prior approval from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand. No material profit remittance hurdles exist; however, outward remittances by a New Zealand banking customer are subject to standard non-resident withholding tax obligations (15%–30% depending on applicable Double Tax Agreement or domestic concession) and to the bank's AML/CFT transaction verification protocols. The Overseas Investment Act 2005 imposes consent requirements only for acquisitions of sensitive New Zealand land, significant business assets above statutory thresholds, or fishing quota; a non-dilutive revenue-based financing fund investing in digital brands through contractual financing arrangements does not trigger this regime. The NZD is not subject to mark-to-market conversion restrictions, nor are there custodian requirements for foreign currency holdings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no export proceeds surrender rules, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory time limit for repatriation of export receipts. Exporters, including fintech financing funds receiving royalties from cross-border merchants, may lawfully retain foreign currency balances in New Zealand foreign currency accounts indefinitely. The only obligations are statistical and monitoring in nature: transactions exceeding NZD 10,000 must be reported through the underlying bank for the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's Balance of Payments survey, and all reporting entities must maintain records of the economic substance of receipt/disbursement flows for at least five years under the AML/CFT Act. No requirement exists to convert export earnings into NZD.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (NZD) supplemented by Foreign Currency Account (USD) for royalty disbursement and FX treasury management
Capital Escrow Account governed by a bank-facility trust deed, plus Operational Account
Operational Account with Direct Debit / ACH clearing integration and treasury-limit facility for FX forwards
Financing Escrow Account for revenue-based lending programmes

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for operational payment flows and Low for statutory capital escrow. New Zealand does not maintain a distinct Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensing class comparable to the European Union regime. Cross-border digital payment providers operate in New Zealand as registered financial service providers under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and, where they hold client funds, as reporting entities under the AML/CFT Act supervised by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand. Wise (Wise Payments NZ Limited), Airwallex (NZ) Limited, and similar API-driven multi-currency providers are legally viable for merchant mass payouts, expense management, and rapid cross-border settlement, but none may lawfully operate a deposit-taking Capital Escrow Account equivalent to that of a Registered Bank. Consequently, the treasury architecture mandates a Registered Bank for the escrow/statutory layer and permits a licensed fintech FSP only as an aggregation and disbursement interface, never as the custodian of client capital.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The AML/CFT Act 2009 does not statutorily require face-to-face identification; nevertheless, New Zealand Tier-1 banks apply an enhanced due diligence matrix that, for a non-resident Cook Islands International Company, normally requires at least one natural-person director or the fund's New Zealand-resident compliance officer to undergo a certified video interview, with identity documents independently verified by a New Zealand notary public or a registered AML/CFT reporting entity, and a local legal counsel certificate confirming corporate existence and signatory authority. ASB and Kiwibank in practice mandate an in-person interview at an Auckland or Wellington branch for tax-exempt offshore International Companies. Strategic recommendation: the fund should appoint a New Zealand-resident administrator or trust-services provider to complete a branch-based identity interview and to serve as the bank correspondence agent, thereby eliminating onboarding delays, accommodating remote board signatories, and satisfying the bank's expectation of a physical nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore Cook Islands International Company bearing a 'Tax Exempt Zone' classification triggers the bank's adverse-media, sanctions, and offshore-shell probability filter.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete defence pack comprising: (a) Certificate of Incorporation and current Certificate of Good Standing from the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission; (b) the International Company constitution and, if applicable, the underlying trust deed; (c) an economic-substance memorandum evidencing active revenue-based financing trade; (d) two years of audited financial statements; (e) a legal opinion confirming compliance with the International Companies Act 2020–21 and absence of nominee anomalies; and (f) a source-of-funds and source-of-wealth report identifying every ultimate beneficial owner to the level of natural persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity ACH/Direct-Debit outbound payments to numerous digital-brand merchants in consumer e-commerce raise layering, mule-account, and structured-transaction red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The fund must lodge: (a) a board-approved AML/CFT compliance programme operated by a designated New Zealand AML/CFT Compliance Officer; (b) merchant onboarding standards incorporating OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening and politically-exposed-person checks; (c) live transaction-monitoring architecture with velocity limits, counterparty risk scoring, and unusual-activity escalation protocols; (d) executed Revenue-Based Financing Agreements and board resolutions authorising each disbursement class; and (e) an external auditor's letter confirming segregation of client funds and the integrity of the collection ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty-financing collections are recharacterised by the bank's product governance committee as unlicensed lending or debt-collection activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a New Zealand legal opinion under the Credit Contracts and Consumer Finance Act 2003 (CCCFA) establishing that the fund lends exclusively to registered business entities and therefore qualifies for the business-lending exclusion in section 16 of the CCCFA; annex the ISIC-6499 classification assessment and, where applicable, Personal Property Securities Register (PPSR) filings recording the fund's security interest in merchants' receivables.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership is layered through Cook Islands and New Zealand trust arrangements, obstructing transparency for the bank's KYC/UBO engine.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a complete trust pack: trust deed, deeds of appointment and retirement of trustees, written trustee resolutions, current registers of members and directors, trust distribution policy, any New Zealand Companies Office beneficial-ownership disclosure, and a notarised source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statement for each protector and beneficiary. Where the overseas jurisdiction withholds access to beneficial ownership registries, a certificated attorney-at-law letter from the Cook Islands providing the equivalent information must be included.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward capital injections from investors or lending providers must be executed as SWIFT MT103/MT202 messages to the fund's New Zealand Registered Bank account. The payment instruction must include the fund's legal name and account number, the bank's SWIFT/BIC, a balance-of-payments purpose code designated by the bank — either 'Direct Investment – Equity' or 'Direct Investment – Intercompany Lending' as applicable — and a non-ambiguous remittance field referencing the executed Subscription Agreement, Capital Call Notice, or Intercompany Loan Agreement. The originating bank must send the wire from the investor's own account; third-party or cash-deposit wires are rejected. Any transaction equal to or exceeding NZD 10,000 attracts records and verification requirements; amounts exceeding NZD 500,000 will ordinarily trigger enhanced due diligence, including a governing-body resolution, an ultimate-beneficial-owner certificate, and confirmation that no politically exposed person is involved. Intercompany loans from connected entities must be supported by a formal loan agreement with commercial-rate interest to preserve the debt characterisation and to enable future interest deductions if the borrower becomes New Zealand-resident. No Reserve Bank approval is required for the inward capital injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic disbursements to New Zealand digital-brand merchants settle through the Bulk Electronic Clearing System (BECS) using Direct Debit on merchant-signed ACH mandates and, for same-day high-value payments, through the CorePlus high-value clearing system operated by the New Zealand Clearing Association with final settlement across Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) balances at the Reserve Bank of New Zealand. Cross-border merchant disbursements are routed as SWIFT MT103 remittances via the bank's correspondent network (for example, JPMorgan Chase or Citibank for USD) including ISO 20022 structured remittance advice, or through Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) where a supplier requires documentary protection. For recurring multi-currency mass payouts to digital brands in multiple overseas jurisdictions, the fund may instruct a licensed fintech FSP (Wise or Airwallex) to become the payment processor, with the NZD funding leg held in the Registered Bank account; final beneficial delivery into each merchant's local clearing system is effected by the FSP's licensed subsidiaries. Every outbound disbursement must reconcile to the merchant receivable ledger and to PPSR-registered security interests, and any wire referencing 'royalty income' must be supported by the underlying Revenue-Based Financing Agreement to avoid adverse classification as an unlicensed money-service business.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Outright FX Forward (NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/AUD) documented under ISDA 1998 FX Definitions and a confirmed Credit Support Annex
Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) for exotic currency pairs where physical delivery is operationally impractical, settled in US Dollars through a permitted offshore bank counterparty
FX Swap (simultaneous spot purchase and forward sale, or vice versa) for commercial treasury liquidity corridor management
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swap (CCIRS) aligning long-term revenue-based financing liabilities with funding-currency cash flows
Vanilla Over-The-Counter FX Options, including zero-cost collars and participating forwards, acquired on a buy-side basis only
NZD/USD Exchange-Traded Currency Futures for margin-efficient micro-hedging of merchant settlement volume and basis-risk adjustment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (including confirmation of directors, shareholders, registered office, and address for service)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (NZ Companies Register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary of incorporation; for registered overseas companies, within one month after the applicable balance date used for New Zealand financial reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of approximately NZD 200; failure to file for two or more consecutive years authorises the Registrar to initiate administrative strike-off after notice; directors and officers may be liable on summary conviction to fines up to NZD 10,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: General Purpose Financial Statements (GPFS) where audit or financial reporting mandate is triggered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after balance date; if filed with the Annual Return, due on the Annual Return filing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-delivery is an offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and may result in infringement fees, court-ordered fines, and continuing non-compliance may be treated as grounds for administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Confirmation of registered office and address for service (annual component of the Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the Annual Return; any change during the year must be notified within 10 working days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a registered office in New Zealand or to notify a change is an offence; if the company cannot be contacted, the Registrar may remove it from the register after due notice.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to FMC reporting entities and to companies that do not qualify as 'small' under the Companies Act 1993 safe-harbour test; a small company has at least two of the following: total assets not exceeding NZD 3 million, turnover not exceeding NZD 10 million, or 50 or fewer full-time employees. A tax-exempt International Company with no New Zealand business activity and no FMC reporting status is generally outside the audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Tier 1 for-profit reporting entities apply New Zealand equivalents to IFRS (NZ IFRS); Tier 2 entities apply NZ IFRS with reduced disclosure (NZ IFRS RDR). A non-resident and tax-exempt International Company that is not required to file New Zealand GPFS may maintain accounts under IFRS or the accounting framework of its incorporation jurisdiction for internal and investor purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not currently require a separate annual UBO return for ordinary tax-exempt International Companies. The member register must be updated on every share transfer, and the Annual Return confirms current shareholders and directors. Under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership Information) Amendment Act 2024, once in force, companies must obtain, hold, and confirm beneficial ownership information at the annual return date, including any natural person owning or controlling 25% or more of the shares or voting rights.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $4,500 - $15,000 per year if audit is triggered; nil if full exemption applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for a Cook Islands International Company (IC) operating in the statutory tax-exempt zone under the International Companies Act 1981; residual domestic corporate income tax rate of 20% applies only to non-exempt local-source income if IC status is revoked.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exemption from corporate income tax, dividend withholding tax, interest withholding tax, royalty withholding tax, and stamp duty; 20-year tax holiday assurance from the Cook Islands Government (extendable for a further 20 years); no capital gains tax; no estate duty; no GST/VAT for International Companies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Return and Declaration of Compliance (Form IC-AR) filed through the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission e-Portal via the licensed registered agent; supplementary CIT-1 Corporate Income Tax Return (only if tax-exempt status is lost) filed with the Cook Islands Revenue Management Division.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual Return: within 90 days of the incorporation anniversary date (statutory annual fee date); CIT-1 (if applicable): within 90 days after the fiscal year-end or on the date prescribed by the Revenue Management Division.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A - Company Identification and Registered Office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IC name, company number, registered office address in Rarotonga, registered agent name and contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficial owners must disclose a valid address for service of process to the registered agent; the registered agent is required to maintain but not publicly file this information.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identity of ultimate beneficial owners, shareholding percentages, and source of funds for the royalty financing fund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners must provide certified passport copies and proof of address to the agent for AML/KYC file; information is subject to inspection by the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C - Annual Fee Schedule and Compliance Confirmation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of payment of the prescribed annual government fee and declaration of compliance with the International Companies Act 1981.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered agent remits the fee on behalf of non-resident owners; no foreign currency restriction applies but Cook Islands Dollars (CI$, pegged 1:1 to NZ$) are accepted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule R - Royalty and Financing Receipts (Voluntary)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed statement of non-dilutive revenue-based financing collections and royalty streams, proving the passive and exempt character of the IC's income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the geographical source of each counterparty payment; any payments sourced from New Zealand digital brands must be excluded from the exempt income position to avoid inadvertent NZ source taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of assessable income, allowable deductions, and gross tax at 20% for any non-exempt trading or domestic-source revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the IC inadvertently engages in domestic Cook Islands or New Zealand trading activities, an appointed Cook Islands tax agent must file; non-resident directors remain responsible for accurate certification.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late Annual Return filing: CI$50 per month late fee, capped at CI$500, plus risk of strike-off and deregistration for non-payment of annual fees; late CIT-1 (if applicable): 20% surcharge on unpaid tax, monthly late payment penalty of 2% per month up to 100% of tax, and criminal liability for knowingly false declarations under the Crimes Act 1969.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on dividends paid by a Cook Islands International Company to non-resident shareholders (full statutory exemption under the International Companies Act 1981); residual statutory non-resident dividend withholding tax of 15% applies only to dividends paid by domestic Cook Islands companies not enjoying IC status.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No withholding tax arises at source on IC distributions, so a treaty relief application is not required in the Cook Islands. For any residual non-exempt dividend, the recipient must: (a) obtain a Cook Islands Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Revenue Management Division, (b) complete the domestic withholding declaration form before payment, and (c) submit the TRC to the paying company's registered agent or tax office. The Cook Islands has no comprehensive double taxation agreement with New Zealand applicable to IC dividends; the IC must not unilaterally claim NZ treaty benefits. Recipients resident in New Zealand should apply New Zealand's foreign dividend exemption to the IC distribution rather than credit relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% withholding tax on royalties and interest paid by a tax-exempt Cook Islands International Company; absent the IC exemption, the statutory gross-basis non-resident withholding rate for royalties and interest sourced from a domestic Cook Islands company is 15% for each category.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No formal transfer pricing statute applies to Cook Islands International Companies; however, prudent practice mandates preparation of a Local File and Master File where all related-party cross-border transactions—including subordinated royalty financing advances and intercompany funding—exceed CI$1,000,000 (Cook Islands Dollar, pegged 1:1 to New Zealand Dollar) annually, aligned with OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines for Financial Transactions (2022).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Cook Islands has not enacted Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) directly comparable to BVI/Cayman; however, the jurisdiction is subject to OECD Global Forum review and has committed to implementing economic substance requirements for geographically mobile financial activities, including financing and leasing. The royalty financing fund must demonstrate adequate substance in Rarotonga: a physical registered office, at least two resident directors, documented board meetings where financing decisions are made, an operational bank account with discretionary fund management, and complete accounting records covering the non-dilutive revenue-based financing and royalty streams. Failure to maintain substance exposes the IC to recharacterization as a shell by New Zealand or foreign tax authorities under general anti-avoidance doctrines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the IC to earn New Zealand-sourced trading income from digital brands disguised as passive royalty or revenue-based financing receipts, or asserting the 0% exempt status while deriving domestic Cook Islands-source commercial revenue through undisclosed local activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of International Company status; assessment at the 20% corporate income tax rate; imposition of late payment penalties up to 100% of the tax and daily interest at 2% per month; criminal fines under the Cook Islands Income Tax Act 1997 and Crimes Act 1969; mandatory disclosure under automatic exchange of information agreements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false declarations become personally liable for unpaid corporate tax through piercing of the corporate veil; civil restitution orders; travel bans pending the completion of tax investigations; imprisonment for up to 5 years for tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the IC as a pure phantom with no physical registered office, no resident decision-makers, no operating bank account, and no substance documentation while routing high-volume financing transactions through ACH and wire rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of general anti-avoidance rules recharacterizing the IC as a sham; denial of the 0% exempt rate; deregistration by the Financial Supervisory Commission; adverse OECD Global Forum rating triggering cross-border tax investigations in New Zealand and Australia; potential inclusion in automatic exchange of information (CRS) filings exposing beneficial owners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director disqualification orders; personal liability for restitution to the tax authority for the amount of tax evaded; extradition risk and international travel bans under mutual legal assistance treaties; imprisonment up to 7 years for fraudulent concealment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Counter-Terrorist Financing Breach in Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an unlicensed non-dilutive revenue-based financing fund with direct debit ACH and wire transfer rails without an approved AML/CFT compliance programme, customer due diligence files, or suspicious transaction reporting, given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced classification under the Banking AML Risk Tier.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under the Cook Islands AML/CFT Act 2019 applicable to reporting entities: financial penalties up to CI$1,000,000 for non-compliance; mandatory closure of payment rails; revocation of any financial services authorization; criminal prosecution for unlicensed financial service provision where fund activity crosses the licensing threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal liability for money laundering offences where they knowingly accepted undisclosed or tainted funds; imprisonment up to 10 years; asset forfeiture and confiscation orders; travel bans and extradition exposure to requesting states.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Thin Capitalization Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the cross-border royalty financing fund with excessive related-party debt bearing non-arm's-length interest rates, or allocating economic profits to the Cook Islands IC without commensurate funding and risk-bearing functions, thereby eroding the tax base of the counterparty jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: If the counterparty is a New Zealand resident, the New Zealand Inland Revenue may apply transfer pricing adjustments under the Income Tax Act 2007 (sections GC 13-GC 16) and thin capitalization rules (section FE 6), imputing additional taxable income and denying interest deductions; penalties of up to 150% of the resultant tax shortfall for documented transfer pricing failure plus use-of-money interest; equivalent adjustments may be made by any treaty partner under OECD Pillar Two rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign incorrect transfer pricing documentation face personal liability for penalties in certain jurisdictions; civil proceedings for reimbursement of corporate tax liabilities; disqualification from serving as directors of international companies; travel bans where criminal tax evasion is established.
